ios.desc:
Go on. Fuel Up. Earn More. Pay Less.

The Exxon Mobil Rewards+ app is your secure, contactless way to pay at the pump or in-store—while earning valuable rewards points every time you fill up or shop at participating Exxon™ and Mobil™ stations.

Why Choose Exxon Mobil Rewards+™?
•      Get up to $5 in points after your first purchase using the App
•	Earn points on fuel, snacks, drinks, and car washes¹
•	Save 10¢ per gallon every day with Exxon Mobil Direct Debit+

How It Works
•	Download the app
•	Create an account
•	Add your preferred payment method
•	Start earning rewards on every eligible purchase

Key Features
•	Pay Securely: Use Apple Pay², credit/debit cards, or Exxon Mobil 
Direct Debit+ & Smart Card+ 
•	Pay at the Pump: Select your pump and fuel grade
•	Pay in Store: Generate a QR code and show it to the cashier
•	Find Stations: Locate nearby Exxon™ and Mobil™ stations
•	Refer Friends: Earn bonus points for every successful referral
•	Get Offers: Unlock exclusive deals on drinks, snacks, and more³
•	Track Rewards: Monitor your points, purchases, and savings
•	Earn Badges: Collect badges and unlock bonus rewards
•	Earn Club Cards: Score more points on multiple in-store purchases
•	My Offers: View exclusive fuel and in-store offers just for you

Accepted Payment Methods
•	Credit & debit cards
•	Apple Pay²
•	Click to Pay
•	Exxon Mobil Smart Card+⁴
•	Exxon Mobil Direct Debit
•	Exxon Mobil BusinessPro™ Card
•	WEX Fleet Cards

Save more with Exxon Mobil Smart Card+ & Direct Debit+ Enroll through the app and save 10¢ per gallon every day⁴.

Disclaimers 
¹ Points can be redeemed for savings on future purchases.
² Apple Pay not valid for in-store app payments; exclusions apply.
³ Offers available at participating locations.
⁴ Subject to credit approval and terms.

For FAQs and full program details, visit: exxon.com/en/rewards-program

quotes.text:
Why isn't the PIN pad on a touch screen?

When working with credit cards and chip/PIN systems the entry of the PIN needs to be secure.  This usually means the scanning lines from the keypad go directly to a security-hardened subprocessor inside the pump - the same one reading the PAN from the EMV chip or magstripe.  Then the PIN/PAN block is encrypted and sent off to the application processor and/or bank to complete the transaction.

If PIN entry was offloaded to the application processor, that processor would need to be audited to make sure of certain requirements (PIN isn't sniffable, it isn't held in RAM after deallocation, encryption isn't breakable, etc).  At the end of the day it pretty much has to be as hardened as the little subprocessor attached to the EMV reader, except any change to the app now needs to be recertified like the subprocessor is.

PCI is beginning to come around to allowing PIN entry on non-secure devices, see the following standard for more information:

https://blog.pcisecuritystandards.org/new-pci-software-pin-entry-on-cots-standard

Or why not allow people to place their orders from their own screens?

This exists.

https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/exxon-mobil-speedpass/id668175318?mt=8

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.webmarketing.exxonmpl
quotes.story_title: The Mystery of Why Gas Pump Interface Design Sucks So Badly
